content: 1. Begin by removing all personal items, such as jewelry, watches, cell phones, pens, and any other accessories, to ensure they do not interfere with the donning process or compromise the sterility of the personal protective equipment (PPE). 2. Proceed to the designated clean area located at the entrance of the isolation unit. This area is specifically prepared to facilitate the safe and proper donning of PPE. 3. Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the PPE set to confirm that all components are available in the correct sizes and that the quality of the equipment is appropriate for the intended use. 4. Perform the procedure of donning PPE under the guidance and supervision of a trained observer or colleague. This ensures that the process is carried out correctly and that no steps are missed. 5. In the changing room, put on a scrub suit and rubber boots. These items serve as the foundational layer of protection and are essential for maintaining hygiene and safety. 6. Put on the coverall, ensuring that it fits properly and provides full coverage of the body. This step is critical for minimizing exposure to infectious agents. 7. Wear a face shield or goggles to protect the eyes and face from potential splashes, droplets, or other hazardous materials. 8. Place a surgical bonnet or hood over the head and neck. The bonnet should cover the neck and sides of the head, and it is preferable to use one that integrates with the face shield for enhanced protection. 9. If rubber boots are unavailable, wear closed shoes that are slip-on, without shoelaces, and fully cover the dorsum of the foot and ankles. Additionally, use shoe covers that are non-slip and preferably impermeable to provide an extra layer of protection. 10. Avoid using adhesive tape to secure gloves to the coverall sleeves. If the gloves or coverall sleeves are not long enough to ensure full coverage, create a thumb or middle finger hole in the coverall sleeve. This modification prevents the forearm from being exposed during wide or extensive movements. 11. Note that some coverall models are designed with built-in finger loops attached to the sleeves. These loops can be used to secure the sleeves in place and prevent them from riding up during use.
